thread:
infra-bot: ALERT: multiple SRV lookup failures observed for service=`internal-search` in region=us-east-1b. Error rate spike 6m > 4x baseline. Affected pods returning DNS NXDOMAIN / timeout. https://metrics.redwood.internal/d/xyz
Devon H: acked. I'm on call and taking this. Paging network oncall @Eli N and platform @Maya P.
Devon H: quick impact note — internal-search is used by realtime-search API; short tail requests failing cause elevated 5xxs for some customer queries.
Maya P: seeing related spikes in kube-dns/consul logs in us-east-1b, aligning with infra-bot window. K8s nodes in that AZ reported increased timeouts to consul agents.
Eli N: i'm tailing the consul raft logs now. can you paste the specific pod ids?
Devon H: pod list from kube: `internal-search-5f6c7d9b-xxx` (x3 in us-east-1b), logs show repeated `SRV lookup timed out` and `dns lookup failed: no such host`.
Maya P: running `kubectl get endpoints -n infra` shows CoreDNS replicas in us-east-1b on a single node group; looks like kube-scheduler placed them all on one unhealthy host after a recent scale-down.
Devon H: hm. runbook step 1: restart coredns pods in the AZ to rebalance. I'll do a rolling restart on the us-east-1b tainted node group.
Devon H: command: ```bash
kubectl -n kube-system get pods -o wide | grep coredns
kubectl -n kube-system delete pod coredns-5f6c7d9b-abc -n kube-system
```
Maya P: I'm also increasing SRV query timeout at the proxy layer for 10m to reduce immediate failures (quick mitigation). Patch pushed to routing sidecar config.
Eli N: confirmed in consul logs: leader keepalive from agent in us-east-1b was delayed and we observed 3 missed heartbeats at 03:07. Might be packet loss on the AZ fabric. Networking team is running BGP health checks now.
Devon H: updating status: rolling restart in progress, watch for restored SRV resolutions. If restarts don't help, fallback plan is to route internal-search traffic to us-east-1a/byp via smart routing policy `route: no-az-affinity`.
Sarah (CS): FYI — Customer A and Customer B reported increased latency and a few 5xxs, CS triage opened. Please keep me posted for customer comms.
Ops Rotation: oncall-bot handed pager to Devon H at 03:12. Devon, are you planning a handoff?
Devon H: i'll own this for the next 60m, then handoff to Maya if it's still active. tagging the incident: internal-dns-srv-az-fabric-0308.
infra-bot: INCIDENT CREATED: internal-dns-srv-az-fabric-0308 | priority=P2 | impact=partial | runbook=https://runbooks.redwood/internal-dns-srv
Maya P: coredns pods restarted, new pods scheduled across us-east-1a and 1b. Initial checks: SRV lookups for internal-search succeed from test pod in us-east-1b now.
Eli N: BGP health shows intermittent flaps on trunk between leaf-12 and spine-3 in us-east-1b. Networking has opened a ticket with cloud provider. We are routing control plane around affected link.
Devon H: rolling metrics — error rate down ~70% from peak, but tail latency still elevated for requests that hit cached stale endpoints. Working TTL/evict: going to lower SRV TTL from 60s -> 10s to force fresh resolution for 5m window.
Maya P: applied SRV TTL override at service mesh level. Also rebalanced consul agents: `systemctl restart consul` on affected nodes and bumped gossip retransmit for 10m.
Sarah (CS): Customer A confirmed reduced errors. They're asking if there was a real outage window length. I'll draft a short note once you confirm mitigation complete.
Devon H: observability shows client error rate returned to baseline at 03:25. marking mitigation successful for now. We'll keep the SRV TTL short and monitor for 30m.
Eli N: cloud provider responded — a regional fabric maintenance event caused transient packet loss affecting that AZ's leaf switches. They have a postmortem pending.
Devon H: handoff to Maya P at 03:35 for continued watch. Maya, please take incident lead and escalate to SEV if recurrence.
Maya P: ack. I'll keep the runbook open and coordinate with networking for provider follow-up. Current steps: 1) keep SRV TTL=10s for 30m 2) maintain coredns spread across nodes 3) monitor consul leader stability 4) prepare route policy rollback after 1h if stable.
Ops Rotation: oncall-bot reminder: please file a short postmortem and include timeline, root cause hypothesis (AZ fabric packet loss -> control plane flaps -> CoreDNS placement skew), customer impact summary and mitigation steps.
Devon H: filing initial incident doc: https://incidents.redwood/internal-dns-srv-1809002468-draft. I'll add logs and command outputs.
Maya P: final note — no config change persisted to production except SRV TTL override and temporary sidecar timeout bump. Rolling those back after stable period.
Sarah (CS): thanks team. i'll prepare customer-facing summary once you share the draft.
infra-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigations in place. status=monitoring.
Maya P: closing active paging; keeping incident open for monitoring. last check-in at 03:56 — all systems normal from us-east-1b perspective.
Devon H: thanks all. I'll attach the runbook steps and timeline in the incident doc.
Maya P: handing final ownership back to Ops Rotation at 04:02.
oncall-bot: Pager rotation: next oncall is Ops Rotation at 04:02.
